summary: Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010), later holding posts at IUPUI and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's and PhD (2014) at Freie Universität Berlin, studying under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch. By 2026, she held research posts at Göttingen Academy and the University of Munich.

Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied with traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Spengel (1838–1905) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (circa 1856–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin, and taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrew Amstutz works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was a member at the Institute for Advanced Study in 2021 and served as Assistant Professor of History at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock as attested in 2022.
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett (born 1961) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (circa 1983–1990) and took up a post at the University of California, Berkeley circa 1995.

Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard G. Salomon), also studying under teachers including Mark Allon and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrew Goudie (born 1945) is a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (circa 1963–1969), and served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and serves as Associate Professor and Director of South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later serving at the Insight Meditation Society, the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and the Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew Ollett (born 1986) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (circa 2008–2010) and Columbia University (circa 2010–2015), becoming an associate professor at the University of Chicago circa 2020.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Princeton University and under teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and held a post as assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago (doctoral supervision by Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins). He holds posts at Smith College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Andrew Sihler (born 1941) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard (1958–1962) and Yale (1962–1967) under Warren Crawford Cowgill, then held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1967 to 1999.

Andrew Watsky (born 1957) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University (PhD circa 1988–1994) and held a post at Vassar College from circa 1995 to 2008.
Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist who earned his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg, supervised by Harunaga Isaacson. He later served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).
